items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I wrote a few things, and I used to go over to his house. I would sit down and play the melody note of the things, man, and he could take his pen and just write right along with you

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Did you usually work with a lyricist, or did you write lyrics of your own?

No, we would work with different individuals that were very good with lyrics, like Andy Razaf, the late and great Andy Razaf, the guy that wrote the lyrics to (unintelligible) "Honeysuckle Rose" with Fats Walker. And he and Fletcher did a lot of things together, but of course, I had the pleasure of living in Los Angeles, pretty close to Andy Razaf, even before he was confined to a wheelchair. And I wrote a few things, and I used to go over to his house. I would sit down and play the melody note of the things,…

I remember one tune called Smooth and Soothing Music. This is the title that he gave a thing that I was fooling around with, and it was a nice little melody. Boy, he wrote 32 bar lyrics in about ten minutes, and it made sense, you know, and it told a little story, you know, and built up to quite a climax. He was a genius.
